prs.title: Editorial: note that TA.prototype.subarray can be customized by Symbol.species
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
This addresses the issue identified in #4014 by @JinDX, but I wrote my own wording that I prefer.

I considered leaving out this detail, especially in light of https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/pull/3450, but since it has potential security implementations if different parts of an implementation make different assumptions here it seemed worth including. I originally tried to enumerate _how_ it could change the behavior but doing so precisely makes it pretty wordy so I didn't bother.

prs.title: Meta: Upgrade ESMeta to v0.8.2
prs.author: jhnaldo
prs.body:
This PR updates the version of ESMeta to [v0.8.2](https://github.com/es-meta/esmeta/releases/tag/v0.8.2) with the following key updates:
* https://github.com/es-meta/esmeta/pull/400 (supports the `≠` form of lookahead restrictions used in #1727)
* https://github.com/es-meta/esmeta/pull/373
* https://github.com/es-meta/esmeta/pull/377

This version removes six algorithms from `esmeta-ignore.json` (`CreateDynamicFunction`, `DecimalEscape[0,1].CapturingGroupNumber`, `IncrementModuleAsyncEvaluationCount`, `PerformEval`, `TimeString`, and `TimeZoneString`), but newly adds two algorithms:
* `LocalTime`
* `MakeFullYear`

Both are false alarms caused by modeling the overflow of Number arithmetic to infinities (https://github.com/es-meta/esmeta/pull/377). For example, in `LocalTime`, ESMeta does not know that `_tv_` is bounded, so it reports that `_tv_ + 𝔽(_offsetMilliseconds_)` may be infinite. We plan to remove them with an interval domain (https://github.com/es-meta/esmeta/issues/354).

prs.title: Editorial: Initialize [[LoadedModules]] in InitializeHostDefinedRealm
prs.author: jungwngkim
prs.body:
[Realm Records](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm-record) have a [[LoadedModules]] field, but nothing initializes it.

#2905 added [[LoadedModules]] to Script Records, Cyclic Module Records, and Realm Records. ParseScript and ParseModule create their records with `[[LoadedModules]]: « »`, but CreateRealm was not updated to initialize the new field, and #3139 carried that omission over when it inlined CreateRealm into InitializeHostDefinedRealm.

This PR initializes the field to a new empty List, as ParseScript and ParseModule already do.

This was found while adding module support to [ESMeta](https://github.com/es-meta/esmeta).
